items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: Lawrence, Carney all them sharps, Ben, all stars. But it wasn't like you say from top to bottom a sheet. Impossible. Because he would write his dream and then them guys would interpret his dream.

ctx.x: They could copy. They could copy note for note. They would go out and buy them records and study religiously. The only time they'd falter, when it comes to individual solos. Because the average colored musician, they couldn't write down how he'd think. Because the average writer would write a skeleton for a number and then make adaptions. Give me two choruses, give me four choruses. Then you would play how you felt. They couldn't write that. Even Duke, they couldn't write it.

He wanted to hear something very beautiful in one of his numbers, he'd write the skeleton and point to Johnny Holiday and say "Play it." And Johnny played the prettiest chorus. Lawrence, Carney all them sharps, Ben, all stars. But it wasn't like you say from top to bottom a sheet. Impossible. Because he would write his dream and then them guys would interpret his dream.
Well, after these guys would improvise on a record and the record would come out, did they play the same solo after that as the ones they played on the record?
